Symptomatic geographic tongue

A 50-person randomized trial reported reduced pain and burning and better healing at later follow-up visits after one PBM session.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A 50-person randomized trial reported reduced pain and burning and better healing at later follow-up visits after one PBM session.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Symptomatic geographic tongue category contains one unique human randomized trial with 50 participants. No additional clinical publication, animal study, review, or in-vitro/ex-vivo experiment was listed. The trial assessed a single treatment and followed participants for 30 days.

Human and clinical evidence

The double-blind randomized trial compared PBM with control treatment in patients with symptomatic geographic tongue. The authors reported reduced pain and burning and improved healing at later assessment points after PBM. This is direct evidence for short-term symptoms, but it comes from one small study and does not establish whether the effect persists, prevents recurrence, or applies to people with different symptom patterns (Saad et al. 2020).

Animal evidence

No relevant animal evidence was identified in the exact category.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone laboratory or ex-vivo study was listed for this indication.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The report describes one application of a 660-nm red diode laser at 25 mW for 120 seconds. Treatment was given once, with observations over 30 days. The database does not record a separate treatment course or a dose-comparison arm, so the trial cannot identify whether repeated sessions or a different setting would change outcomes.

Interpretation

The trial documents improvement in symptoms and healing after one session, but a single study cannot establish a reproducible effect. Evidence is absent on longer-term symptom control and on whether PBM changes the underlying course of geographic tongue.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for short-term pain, burning, and healing outcomes after one PBM session in symptomatic geographic tongue
Publications and records1 unique title

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The rating rests on one small randomized trial with 50 participants, a single treatment, and follow-up of only 30 days. The reported symptom and healing differences are clinically relevant but have not been independently replicated. Larger trials with sham control, prespecified outcomes, and longer follow-up would clarify reliability and recurrence.
